It uses nearly identical language to certify plural labor disputes to the same Board, follows the same sequence from the presidential national-defense finding through referral and investigation, discusses failed bargaining and imminent industrywide production losses, identifies the affected companies, explains the material's importance to defense, and closes by urging maintenance of normal production while the disputes are before the Board. The child adapts this concrete letter structure from steel to aluminum. It appears entirely unlikely ... that the present stalemate could be broken by further bargaining or mediation and conciliation in time to avoid early and serious production losses in this vital industry.","explanation":"Closely parallel account of failed negotiations and the inability of further mediation to avert losses in a vital industry."},{"child_excerpt":"A curtailment of these operations in the aluminum industry would have an immediate and serious impact on many of our defense production programs.","parent_excerpt":"Any curtailment of operations in the steel industry will have an immediate and serious impact on the defense program.","explanation":"Near-verbatim defense-impact justification with the affected material changed."},{"child_excerpt":"The parties of these disputes should cooperate fully in maintaining normal work and production schedules while the disputes are before the Board.","parent_excerpt":"the parties to disputes in the steel industry owe it to the American people to cooperate with their government in maintaining normal work and production schedules while this matter is before the Board.","explanation":"Same closing appeal to preserve normal production during Board proceedings."}]}
